items.statement: Pain/discomfort was the most frequently reported EQ-5D-3L problem in most registers and in the general population at both assessed time points; mobility was most frequent in respiratory failure.
source: Full article, Results, Problems reported on the EQ-5D-3L dimensions, first paragraph and table 2

items.statement: Across specific diagnoses, mean EQ VAS ranged from 45.2 for disc hernia to 88.1 for wrist and hand fracture at baseline, and from 48.9 for pulmonary fibrosis to 83.3 for wrist and hand fracture at follow-up.
source: Full article, Abstract, Results

items.statement: Mean EQ VAS increased in all reported register groups except fracture and respiratory failure; the largest mean increases were in hip and spine patients.
source: Full article, Results, Mean self-assessed EQ VAS score, first paragraph and table 3

items.statement: The PCHC improved category had the largest proportion for most diagnoses, but worsened was largest for respiratory failure and fracture; heart failure had similar improved and worsened proportions.
source: Full article, Results, Paretian Classification of Health Change and figure 1

items.statement: At baseline, diagnoses other than fractures had statistically significantly lower adjusted mean EQ VAS scores than the general population. At follow-up, scores generally improved but remained lower than the general population, except for fracture patients.
source: Full article, Results, paragraph following figure 3

items.statement: Women had statistically significantly lower age-adjusted mean EQ VAS scores in most registers. Reported exceptions were fracture and respiratory failure at baseline and BOA, fracture, heart failure, and respiratory failure at follow-up.
source: Full article, Results, paragraph before table 4

items.statement: Supplementary table S6 was reported as usable EQ-5D-3L reference data for the studied diagnoses, except fracture because its baseline data referred to health before the fracture.
source: Full article, Results, final paragraph before Discussion

items.statement: The authors interpreted the EQ-5D-3L descriptive system and EQ VAS as a common denominator that permits comparisons across National Quality Registers and diagnoses.
source: Full article, Abstract, Conclusions
Full article, Conclusions

items.statement: The authors concluded that the corresponding patterns in EQ-5D-3L problems and EQ VAS scores support the use of patient-reported outcomes to monitor health status and progress in routine clinical care.
source: Full article, Conclusions, paragraphs 1–2

items.statement: Differences in health-related quality of life could arise from different data-collection modes across the National Quality Registers.
source: Full article, Strengths and limitations of this study

items.statement: Comorbidities among patients and morbidities in the general population could affect comparisons, and the study did not fully address this issue.
source: Full article, Discussion, Strengths and limitations, paragraph 1

items.statement: Restricting the main analysis to complete baseline and 1-year follow-up records excluded non-respondents and incomplete records and could introduce selection bias.
